conviction_note: The evidence nets close to zero. The Q3 quarter itself looks in line: Placer same-store visits +1.7% plus 3-4 points of price/mix gives about 3-5% comps against a 3-3.6% bar. The forward read leans slightly negative: Chipotle's CFO said October softened industry-wide, the Street's FY26 6.8% sits above management's 6.5% ceiling, and the stock is +17% in five days. That lean agrees with the +16.5 put skew, so it is probably priced, and 13-15% short interest argues for a squeeze. p_up is 47 against an abs move of 12.5 (the implied 12.1; recent prints were +14, +26 and -17), giving -0.75, close to the findings' sum of -0.4.
bar: Q3 FY26 (12 weeks to about 2026-10-04): revenue $357.4m (Zacks, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ahead-cava-cava-q3-earnings-121505633.html, 2026-10-30) to $358.4m (sweep preview); EPS $0.12 (the same two sources); restaurant revenue $360.25m; restaurant-level profit $83.8m, an implied margin of about 23.3% against 24.6% a year ago; 498 restaurants and 19 openings. Same-restaurant sales consensus 3.6%, with surveyed analysts at about 3% (Investing.com, 2026-11-04, https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/cava-earnings-on-deck-growth-test-amid-fast-casual-headwinds-93CH-5000733). That agrees with roughly 3.0% backed out of the Street's FY26 6.8% and Q4 4.5% (StreetSignal, https://streetsignal.substack.com/p/cava-group-eps-bogeys). The year-ago comp is an easy 1.9%. The company guide was reaffirmed on 2026-08-11 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001639438/000162828026055709/earningsrelease2026q2.htm): FY26 SRS 4.5-6.5%, adj EBITDA $181-191m, RLM 23.7-24.3%, 75-77 net new units. With H1 at about 9.4% (Q1 16 weeks at 9.7%, Q2 12 weeks at 9.0%), the guide implies H2 comps of about -1.2% to +3.1%. The Street sits ABOVE the top of the guide, so the market needs the ceiling raised, not just the floor.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 13-15% of float with about 4 days to cover. Swingtradebot shows 13.40% of a 108m float and 4.34 DTC on an October 2026 page, settlement date not shown (https://swingtradebot.com/equities/CAVA). Massive.com shows 15.85m shares short and 4.0 DTC as of 2026-09-30 (https://massive.com/quote/cava). Earlier readings were Benzinga 12.2% on 2026-08-11 and Equibles 11.0% around August, so the short has been rising. Skew is +16.5 vol points (25d put IV minus call IV), meaning downside is paid. The put/call OI ratio is 0.95 and ATM IV 174%. The event-implied move is 12.11%, but the ATM spread is 37% of mid. The stock is +17.3% over 5 days and +22.2% over 20, up from $52.07 on 2026-10-07, while still 34.7% below its 52-week high. A short this crowded is a squeeze mechanism, so the negatives below are trimmed for it.

findings.finding: Placer.ai (2026-11-02) puts CAVA's calendar-Q3 2026 same-store visits at +1.7% YoY and total visits at +16.3%. On the same series, Q1 read +6.8% when CAVA reported +6.8% traffic, and April and June read about 7.7-7.9% when Q2 reported traffic was +5.3%. That points to Q3 traffic of roughly 0-2%; adding the 3-4 points of price/mix seen in H1 gives comps of about 3-5%, at or slightly above the 3-3.6% consensus. Total visits +16.3% plus about 3.5 points of check gives revenue growth near 20%, a little short of the 22-24% consensus ($357-358m).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Comps lead this name. Q1 2026 comps of 9.7% against 6.2% expected sent the stock +3.1% (the 2026-05-19 print). Q2 comps of 9.0% against 7.6% sent it +14.2% (2026-08-11). Q3 2025 comps of 1.9% against a 2.8% target, with a guide cut, sent it -2.6% (2025-11-04).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a free public series that anyone can read, so it is probably mostly priced. If the market were reading it as a clear beat, consensus comps would have moved above 4% and the skew would not be at +16.5. The total-visits-versus-revenue gap is an inference that no preview makes.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a company number. The Q1 calibration is in Placer's 2026-04-23 post (https://www.pulse.bot/food-and-beverage/news/diverging-paths-what-the-data-reveals-about-cava-and-sweetgreen-placerai-blog-4910485b-e36a-4da6-93f1-fe0ac58696a1/) and the Q2 monthly readings are at https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/sweetgreen-rebounds-cava-keeps-climbing. The two readings (same-store and total visits) come from one document and are merged here for that reason.

findings.finding: Chipotle's CFO said on the 2026-10-28 Q3 call that 'October trends have softened, consistent with the broader industry'. That is the first counterparty read on fast-casual October demand since CAVA last spoke, and October is exactly the quarter-to-date month CAVA will comment on tonight. One preview names 'October running at 5% or better' as the real test.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The forward guide and the quarter-to-date commentary decide this name. The 2025-08-12 print (guide cut) went -16.6% and the 2025-11-04 print (guide cut again) went -2.6%. The 2026-02-24 print (strong FY26 first guide) went +26.4%, and the 2026-08-11 print (CFO: recovering to mid-single digits) went +14.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the put skew is +16.5. But CAVA has rallied 17% in five sessions since Chipotle and Wingstop reported, so the tape reacted to Chipotle's Q3 comp beat, not to its October warning. If the warning were priced, CAVA would not have run up into the print.
findings.independence: This comment is a direct counterparty statement. StreetSignal (https://streetsignal.substack.com/p/cava-group-eps-bogeys) independently says Q3 checks were 'choppy' and that October at 5% or better is the bar. The NRN piece on fast-casual traffic below 1% in 2026 is a broader proxy (https://www.nrn.com/fast-casual/2026-is-the-year-limited-service-restaurants-must-win-back-the-middle-class-consumer).

findings.finding: Baird's store checks, as quoted in a StreetSignal preview, saw an early sales pickup after CAVA's 2026-10-14 'Greek Goddess' menu launch. That is a company-specific Q4 quarter-to-date positive, set against the industry softness Chipotle described.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As above: quarter-to-date commentary moved the stock +14.2% in August 2026 and +26.4% in February 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: It comes from a paywalled sell-side checks note that reached only a paywalled substack excerpt. I could not find a CAVA press release for the launch, so the wire has not carried it. It is likely part of what bid the stock up 17% over five days.
findings.independence: None from a different source; my search for a launch release came back empty. The same document as the Street-bar finding below, but a different fact.

findings.finding: Chipotle's Q3 10-Q (quarter to 2026-09-30) says the comp headwinds that began in July, tied to food-safety concerns, had returned to pre-disruption levels by the end of August, and Chipotle's Q3 comps of +2.1% beat the 1.5% consensus. That corroborates the week-by-week recovery CAVA's CFO described on 2026-08-11, so CAVA's Q3 should be a July trough followed by a recovery, not a sustained hole.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CAVA rallied with the sector after Chipotle (+8.9%) and Wingstop (+17.7%) reported, and was +17.3% over the five days to the seal.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is the read-through behind the 5-day run-up. It is filed small because the recovery date (end of August) is a primary-document fact the previews do not quote.
findings.independence: CAVA's own Q2 call commentary, via TIKR (https://www.tikr.com/blog/the-cyclospora-scare-cost-cava-sales-in-july-august-erased-the-doubt), points the same way.

findings.finding: The Street models FY26 comps at 6.8%, above the 6.5% top of management's guide, and Q4 at 4.5% (StreetSignal, 2026-11-03). The stock has also rebounded about 20% in five sessions. On the August guide arithmetic, holding 4.5-6.5% after Q3 means H2 of -1.2% to +3.1%. So meeting the bar needs a raise to the TOP of the range, and a floor-only raise, the obvious mechanical move once Q3 is booked, would land below the Street.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-11 the guide was reaffirmed, not raised, despite 9% comps, and the stock still rose 14.2% because the quarter-to-date commentary was firm. On 2025-11-04 a guide cut brought only -2.6%. The name has not always punished a merely-held guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The fact that consensus sits above the company's ceiling appears in one paywalled preview, not in the wire copy, which quotes only EPS and revenue. If the market held a guide-anchored bar, it would not have run the stock up 17% into a print where the mechanical outcome is a floor raise.
findings.independence: Jefferies modelled FY26 comps at 6.8% back in May (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/cava-raises-2026-outlook-strong-132300538.html). The guide figures come from the 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001639438/000162828026055709/earningsrelease2026q2.htm). This shares a document with the Baird finding above.

findings.finding: Short interest is about 13-15% of float (15.85m shares as of 2026-09-30, about 4 days to cover) and has risen from about 11-12% in August. A short this crowded supplies a squeeze mechanism on anything better than feared.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The +26.4% reaction in February 2026 and +14.2% in August 2026 came on beats from a heavily shorted base.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is partly covered already: the stock is +17% in 5 days. At 4 DTC enough short remains to amplify a positive guide.
findings.independence: Swingtradebot shows 13.40% of float and 4.34 DTC (https://swingtradebot.com/equities/CAVA). Benzinga shows 12.2% on 2026-08-11 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CAVA/sentiment).

findings.finding: The company's first-ever buyback, up to $100m, was approved on 2026-09-17 and funded from about $323-436m of cash with no debt. Q3 closed around 2026-10-04 and the stock traded at $52-60 between approval and today, so the release or 10-Q will disclose any repurchases made in Q3 and since quarter end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior buyback disclosure exists. The stock reaction to the announcement is not sourced.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is priced. Its execution and pace are not yet known. Against a market cap of about $7bn the effect is small.
findings.independence: The TIKR buyback analysis (https://www.tikr.com/blog/why-is-cava-spending-100-million-to-buy-back-its-own-stock) and the Melius note on cash (https://www.tikr.com/blog/cava-group-has-lost-37-in-6-months-melius-sees-82-upside).

findings.finding: Unit growth is on track: CAVA opened its 500th restaurant on 2026-09-23, against consensus of 498 at period end with 19 Q3 openings. StreetSignal and TIKR's Q2 coverage say new cohorts are outselling the system (productivity above 100%, AUV about $3.1m). That supports the revenue line independently of comps.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Openings have not been a surprise line; the stock trades on comps.
findings.why_not_priced: The restaurant count is public and in consensus, so this is mostly priced. The above-system productivity of the newest cohorts is the part not in the revenue models. It argues against the Placer total-visit inference in the first finding.
findings.independence: Q2 cohort productivity: https://www.tikr.com/blog/cava-q2-earnings-new-store-cohorts-are-outselling-the-system-productivity-tops-100 ; the Street restaurant count comes from the Zacks preview.

findings.finding: Chipotle's Q3 restaurant-level margin fell 120bp, from 24.5% to 23.3%, on labor (25.7% of revenue, up from 25.2%) and promotions. CAVA's consensus already embeds about 23.3% against 24.6% a year ago, a cut of about 130bp, so the industry cost read is roughly in the bar. The risk is that CAVA's higher marketing and labor spend comes in above it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 restaurant-level margin was down 60bp and the stock still rose 14.2%. Margin has been a secondary line for this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Consensus already models a cut of about 130bp, which is visible in the Zacks restaurant-level profit estimate.
findings.independence: The Zacks preview's implied margin (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ahead-cava-cava-q3-earnings-121505633.html). StreetSignal warns that marketing and labor spend could offset the upside.

outside_window.finding: Sweetgreen, CAVA's closest fast-casual comparable, reports Q3 2026 after the close on 2026-11-05. Its read-through lands after this window's exit at that day's close.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Investing.com preview revenue consensus of $317.3m (up 8.6% YoY)
rejected_candidates.detail: Inconsistent with Zacks' $357.4m and the sweep's $358.4m, and with 20% unit growth on a $292m year-ago base. Likely a stale or wrong field. The same article's comps figure (3-3.6%) is kept as the bar.
Sweetgreen reports 2026-11-05 after the close, so the read-through falls after the exit at that day's close.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Placer.ai September 2026 Dining Index: fast-casual visits +2.2% YoY, QSR -2.2%
rejected_candidates.detail: A segment-level version of the CAVA-specific Placer finding (same provider, same quarter), merged into the first finding.

baseline_tension: My slight negative lean agrees with the +16.5 put skew, so it is probably already in the price. The +17% five-day run-up cuts both ways: it raises the bar on the guide (negative) and shows that shorts holding 13-15% of float are being squeezed (positive). Together they keep p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short, 13-15% of float, and a sign agreeing with a strong put skew): the Chipotle-October finding is trimmed from -1.5 to -1.2 and the Street-above-guide finding from -1.0 to -0.8; p_up moves from 46 to 47.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): revenue and EPS each rest on two agreeing sources (Zacks and the sweep preview); comps rest on Investing.com plus arithmetic from StreetSignal's FY and Q4 Street numbers, so the findings are not capped. The $317.3m revenue figure is rejected as contradicted.

Lessons 5 and 3 (proxy sizing, caveats reaching the number): Placer stays small and is merged into one finding because both readings come from one document; the Baird pickup and the Chipotle October softness can both be true and stay as separate signed findings.
Lesson 1 left standing: the reaction runs on guidance and quarter-to-date commentary, so the reported-quarter findings stay small.
